newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Spanish deal to involve Arbed capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Spanish deal to involve Arbed capital increase.

text.p: Steel maker Arbed said on Friday its previously announced deal to buy 35 percent of Spanish steel firm CSI, under which CSI will take a 9.5 percent stake in Arbed, would involve a capital increase for the Luxembourg company.
"CSI will underwrite a capital increase in Arbed, giving the Spanish company a 9.5 percent stake in Arbed," Arbed said in a statement.
Spanish state holding firm AIE said when it announced the deal earlier this week that CSI would pay 36.4 billion pesetas for its 9.5 percent of Arbed.

CSI will also acquire stakes of between 20 and 35 percent in Arbed group companies, including trading firms, service centres, cold rolling and coating lines and stakes in the group's Brazilian interests.

"From the financial point of view the deal will strengthen the consolidated accounts of the Arbed group as they will benefit from the excellent financial position of the Spanish group," the Arbed statement said.

"As a consequence of this deal CSI will become an international company and a partner in a new, reinforced operation, while the strategic position of the Arbed group will be greatly enhanced," it added.

Arbed will acquire the 35 percent in CSI -- Corporacion Siderurgica Integral -- by subscribing to a capital increase in CSI amounting to 31 billion Luxembourg francs. It will also receive warrants to acquire a further 15 percent stake in CSI.
"The structure of the financial transaction" reflects the industrial and strategic objectives pursued, (namely) the achievement of a strong partnership between two groups", the Arbed statement said.

AIE said this week it chose Arbed over rival French bidder Usinor as a strategic partner for CSI because of its plans to increase productivity at the Spanish firm. The deal was formally approved on Friday by the Spanish government.
Arbed said the acquisition would be followed by the implementation of a major long-term investment plan in Spain.

"The projects identified, which total more than 30 billion Luxembourg francs investment by CSI, will translate into substantial productivity gains and increased output for the Spanish steel maker," it said.
The new entity's combined crude steel output will be more than 16 million tonnes a year.

Arbed said the two groups complemented each other in several areas, and said Arbed's know-how would represent a key element in the partnership. The plan also included increased research activity in Spain.
Geographically, the new group would benefit from the "commercial integration achieved through Sidstahl, Europrofil and the TradeARBED global network."
Arbed said the CSI privatisation process will continue with the sale of 15 to 25 percent of the company to several, mainly Spanish, partners, and the rest would be floated on the stock market.
It said CSI was active in long products and in heavy plates, and had a flat products division that was well integrated downstream, particularly in the coating sector.
CSI was also active in tinplate, which Arbed did not produce, and held a stake in a mini mill, ACB, which used new thin slab casting technology.
